t:
(a) 
Section 16 of the Peace Corps Act, as amended, which relates to appointment of persons serving under prior law, section 20 of the Peace Corps Act, as amended, which relates to moratorium on student loans, section 21 of the Peace Corps Act, as amended, which amends the Civil Service Retirement Act, and title II of the Act, which relates to Internal Revenue Code and Social Security Act amendments, are hereby repealed.
 
    (b) 
Such repeal shall not be deemed to affect amendments contained in such provisions and the application of the amendments contained in the title. All determinations, authorization, regulations, orders, contracts, agreements, and other actions issued, undertaken, or entered into under authority of the provisions of law repealed by subsection (a) shall continue in full force and effect until modified by appropriate authority.

fable.w: This section repeals several Peace Corps Act provisions and includes a savings clause that keeps existing actions in force. The tempting reading is that the words "regulations" and "agreements" signal rulemaking or outside coordination, but they only preserve past actions and grant no new rulemaking authority. No party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.
fable.s: All determinations, authorization, regulations, orders, contracts, agreements, and other actions issued, undertaken, or entered into under authority of the provisions of law repealed by subsection (a) shall continue in full force and effect until modified by appropriate authority.

qwen_block.w: This section repeals specific provisions of the Peace Corps Act and preserves existing administrative actions. It does not establish any new process for consulting with or coordinating with non-federal entities, nor does it create advisory bodies, public comment periods, or rights to sue. The text deals entirely with internal statutory changes and the continuity of federal administrative actions.
qwen_block.s: Section 16 of the Peace Corps Act, as amended, which relates to appointment of persons serving under prior law, section 20 of the Peace Corps Act, as amended, which relates to moratorium on student loans, section 21 of the Peace Corps Act, as amended, which amends the Civil Service Retirement Act, and title II of the Act, which relates to Internal Revenue Code and Social Security Act amendments, are hereby repealed.

opus.w: This section repeals several parts of the Peace Corps Act and includes a savings clause that keeps past determinations, regulations and agreements in force. It does not authorize or require new rulemaking, a hearing, a comment period, consultation with outside parties, or a right to sue. The words "regulations" and "agreements" refer only to actions already taken, not to any future process that would involve outsiders.
opus.s: All determinations, authorization, regulations, orders, contracts, agreements, and other actions issued, undertaken, or entered into under authority of the provisions of law repealed by subsection (a) shall continue in full force and effect until modified by appropriate authority.
opus.b: I'm labelling this section "No". It might look like participation because it mentions "regulations", "contracts" and "agreements". But it only keeps existing actions in force after the repeal. It does not give any agency the power to make new rules, and it brings no one outside the federal government into a decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section repeals specific provisions of the Peace Corps Act and states that existing determinations, regulations, and agreements remain in effect. It does not create any new requirement for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The mention of 'agreements' and 'contracts' refers to the continuation of existing legal instruments, not a participatory process for decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: All determinations, authorization, regulations, orders, contracts, agreements, and other actions issued, undertaken, or entered into under authority of the provisions of law repealed by subsection (a) shall continue in full force and effect until modified by appropriate authority.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "agreements" or "contracts" mentioned in subsection (b) imply ongoing participation or consultation with outside parties. However, the text merely states that existing legal instruments remain in force; it does not establish a new process for outside parties to participate in federal decision-making. The section is purely about the repeal of statutes and the continuity of existing administrative actions, which are internal government matters or pre-existing legal obligations, not new participatory mechanisms.
